title: AI security catalogue entry
description: One entry describing a documented, evidenced attack on an AI system. data/entries/<id>.yml is the single source of truth; everything published is generated from these files.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, unique across the catalogue. Never renamed once published: the id is the public anchor of the entry.

title.description: Short factual title. No hype, no marketing adjectives, no angle brackets.

tier.description: 1 = confirmed in the wild. 2 = demonstrated. 3 = theoretical. When uncertain between two tiers, choose the lower number.

attack_class.description: Exactly one class. Entries that plausibly fit two classes must be resolved with the tie-break rule in docs/TAXONOMY.md before filing.

target.description: What was affected: named product, component, or ecosystem. 'LLM applications in general' is acceptable for a class-level finding but must be justified in impact.

date.description: Disclosure date exactly as the primary source states it, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Never inferred, never rounded to a nicer date.

summary.description: 2-4 sentences in the curator's own words: what happened and how it was disclosed. Never a paraphrase close enough to the source to be a substitute copy.

impact.description: What the attacker gained, or could gain, stated precisely. For tier 1 entries this field must also state that the source confirms real-world exploitation or affected users, and cite which source says so.

mitigation.description: What a defender can actually do. 'None known' is an acceptable, honest value and is preferred to padding.

url.description: http/https only. Plain http is rejected because it cannot be a trustworthy reference.

kind.description: primary = the advisory, vendor postmortem, CVE record, or original research that states the finding. secondary = news coverage, commentary, aggregator. A secondary source may be added alongside a primary one, never instead of it.

title.description: Title of the source as published, so a reader can recognise it before clicking.

sources.description: At least one primary source is required for tier 1 and tier 2. Tier 3 requires at least one source but it may be a paper or talk.

cve.description: Optional. Only CVE identifiers the source itself states. Omit the key entirely rather than leaving it empty or guessing an id.

last_verified.description: The date the curator fetched each source and confirmed the entry against its text. Not the entry's disclosure date.
